note: Window agent m1200-m1101, 2 Nov 2026. Pages opened: Kingdom of Kush, Ramesses VI, Babylonia, Mycenaean Greece, Middle Assyrian Empire (the Second Dynasty of Isin page returned nothing usable). Egypt: the 'wrong' keyframe -1240 (spec = its own Cliopatria shape, -1240..-1151) was unioned into the keyframe of record at -1200 and -1150, so the dossier's own loss of the Dongola Reach at -1200 was undone and 188 cells in the Sudan stayed Egyptian until the -1150 snap; a 9-cell box of the -1500 shape lying outside the gazetteer's 'Nubia' stayed Egyptian to the end; ten Lebanese cells stayed Egyptian after the Canaan vassalage ended. Assyria: the page dates a first period of decline c. 1206-1115 in which Assyria was restricted mostly to its heartland, so the heartland replaces the 1,500-cell empire for -1200..-1115 and the empire shape starts at Tiglath-Pileser I's accession in -1114. Mycenaean Greece: the carved-out palace states of Pylos and Mycenae left 4 and 13 cells of nobody's land inside the Peloponnese when they ended. Babylonia: eight cells (seven of the Babylon area) stayed with Elam from 1158 for good.

correction.text: the Assyrian heartland around Assur, Nineveh and Arbela (the dossier's own heartland shape, assyria_-1055), for the first period of decline, -1206..-1115

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier keeps Cliopatria's 467,282 km2 empire for -1200..-1151 because 'page silent on frontiers 1207-1115'. The page is not silent: its infobox has 'First period of decline: c. 1206-1115 BC'; after Tukulti-Ninurta I's murder 'Assyria became restricted mostly to just the Assyrian heartland'; Ashur-nirari III and Enlil-kudurri-usur 'were unable to maintain Assyrian power', Ninurta-apal-Ekur (c. 1191-1179) was 'unable to do much about the collapse of the empire', and Ashur-dan I (c. 1178-1133) only 'improved somewhat' the situation with a campaign against Babylonia, while Ashur-resh-ishi (1132-1115) 'began to reverse the decades of Assyrian decline'. Tiglath-Pileser I (from 1114) then reconquered 'the cities of northern Syria, which had ceased to pay tribute decades prior'. So the empire shape is drawn from 1114 (keyframe assyria_-1150 below), and the heartland shape, the one the dossier uses for 1055-1001, stands in for -1200..-1115. The dossier's years -1200..-1151 become -1200..-1115 here.

keyframe_overrides.why: Same shape as the dossier (verdict ok), but valid from 1114 instead of -1150: the page dates the reconquest to Tiglath-Pileser I (1114-1076): 'In his first year as king, Tiglath-Pileser defeated the Mushki', he 'waged war on the Nairi people in the Armenian highlands', 'The cities of northern Syria, which had ceased to pay tribute decades prior, were reconquered', and he claimed conquests 'to the other side of the Euphrates River' from his accession year to his fifth regnal year. Nothing in the page puts any of this before 1114; the Ashur-dan I and Ashur-resh-ishi paragraphs name only Babylonia. Cliopatria's -1100 shape (the dossier's assyria_-1100, valid -1100..-1056) is the same extent, so the seam at -1100 does not move.

events.note: 1153: Babylonia returns under Dynasty IV from Isin. Babylonia page: 'Marduk-kabit-ahheshu (1155-1139 BC) to establish the Dynasty IV of Babylon, from Isin' and of Nebuchadnezzar I (c. 1121-1103) 'He fought and defeated the Elamites and drove them from Babylonian territory'. The dossier's -1153 gain and Elam's -1153 loss move 527 of the 534 cells Elam took in 1155; eight cells (seven round Babylon, Babil 5 and Wasit 2, and one near the Basra marshes) stay Elamite from 1153 to the end of the window and beyond, as a detached speck inside Iraq: they belong to Cliopatria's -1240 Babylonia shape (134,294 km2, the dossier's keyframe -1220..-1201) and not to its -1200 shape (132,636 km2) that the gain uses; the region here is the union of the two shapes. This gives them back to Babylonia with the rest.
